problem_summary.summary: Determine whether the words in a space-separated string match a pattern through a one-to-one mapping from letters to words.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: lowercase pattern and a string of lowercase words separated by single spaces. Return true only if the word count matches and the mapping is bijective.
constraints: s contains lowercase English letters and single separating spaces, with no leading or trailing spaces

brute_force.explanation: Split s into words, then compare every pair of positions. A pair must repeat the same pattern character exactly when it repeats the same word.
brute_force.correctness_idea: A bijection preserves equality and inequality for every pair of positions. The pairwise test captures both mapping directions, and the initial length check ensures every pattern position has a word.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n^2 * L) worst case, where n is the word count and L bounds the cost of comparing words.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(total input size) for the split word array.

optimized.explanation: Split into words and maintain maps in both directions: letter to word and word to letter. Reject a conflicting existing mapping; otherwise store both mappings.
optimized.correctness_idea: The forward map enforces one word per letter, while the reverse map prevents two letters from sharing a word. Checking both at every aligned position is sufficient for a bijection.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n + |s|) expected, including splitting and expected constant-time map operations.
optimized.space_complexity: O(n + |s|) auxiliary for the split words and distinct mappings.

steps.condition: The number of words equals the number of pattern letters.
steps.action: Initialize empty forward and reverse maps.

steps.condition: Neither mapping conflicts; both are absent.
steps.action: Store a to sun and sun to a.

steps.condition: Neither mapping conflicts; both are absent.
steps.action: Store b to moon and moon to b.

steps.condition: Existing forward and reverse mappings match this pair.
steps.action: Keep both mappings; finish and return true.

edge_cases.handling: The length check returns false before mapping.

edge_cases.case: One letter is paired with two words
edge_cases.handling: The forward map detects the mismatch.

edge_cases.case: Two letters are paired with one word
edge_cases.handling: The reverse map detects the collision.
